rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL ZONES (AGRIZONES) TO ENHANCE PRODUCTION, PROVIDING THE NECESSARY SUPPORT SERVICES SUCH AS IRRIGATION, FARM-TO-MARKET ROADS, POST-HARVEST EQUIPMENT AND FACILITIES, RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT, AGRICULTURAL EXTENSION, FARM CREDIT ACCESS, SMALL FARMER COOPERATIVES, AND OTHER AGRICULTURAL INFRASTRUCTURES , APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Agricultural Productivity enhancement Program Act of 1996" Rationale: The proposed bill identifies and focuses government support on certain priority areas whose agro-climatic features and market conditions are favorable for producing, processing,and marketing specific products. It encourages farmers and fishers to produce specific crops, such as rice, corn, coconut, sugar, tobacco, high value crops; livestocks, and fishery products only in areas that have the comparative advantage in producing such commodities. > Is premised on the principles of: (1) global competitiveness ; (2) participatory development process; (3) sustainable development; and (4) rational use of resources. Identifies the proposed agrizones.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 1996-08-01

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE CASH GIFT FOR ALL OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES OF THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, INCLUDING BARANGAY OFFICIALS, TO FIVE THOUSAND PESOS (P5,000.00), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIX THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED EIGHTY SIX AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: INCREASES the cash gift for all officials and employees of the national government and local government units to FIVE THOUSAND PESOS (P5,000.00) to be implemented over a period of THREE (3) YEARS, as follows: (1) P2,500.00 - Christmas Year 1996; (2)An additional P1,250.00 - Christmas Year 1997; (3) An additional P1,250.00 - Christmas Year 1998. Entitles officials and employees who have rendered less than four (4) months of service from January 1 to October 31 of each year and who are employedas of October 31 of the same year with the following cash gifts. Length of Service: 3 months but less than 4 months - P2,000.00; 2 months but less than 3 months - P1,500.00; 1 month but less than 2 months - P1,000.00; Less than one month - P500.00.
rows.status: Substituted by HB08035

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REVISE THE SCHEDULE OF FAIR MARKET VALUES OF RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS, AS WELL AS THE ASSESSMENT LEVELS, SO AS TO EXEMPT FAMILY HOMES, THE FAIR MARKET VALUE OF WHICH IS NOT OVER P300,000, FROM REAL PROPERTY TAX, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991'
rows.abstract: Considers FAMILY HOME as a tie which binds and strengthens the Filipino family - the foudnation of the nation. Is premised on the following: (1) the rapid increase in real proeprty valution would ultimately lead to almost confiscatory higher taxes and could spell doom for the family home; (2) the take home pay of low-salaried employees is not sufficient to finance their basic necessities, thus, the Filipino family is going to be unstable because of the damger of losing their common bond which is the family home. Provides for the following REVISED schedule of Fair Market Values of RESIDENTIAL buildings and assessment levels: (see abs. 37 for the table). Provides further that the EXEMPTION shall apply only to the property which is used excluusively as DWELLING of claimant's family and is not used in whole or in aprt for any COMMERCIAL purpose.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE POSITION OF FISHERIES OFFICER IN COASTAL MUNICIPALITIES, CITIES AND PROVINCES AND IN THOSE WHERE A SUBSTANTIAL NUMBER OF THE INHABITANTS OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNIT CONCERNED IS ENGAGED IN INLAND FISHING OR THE CULTURE OF FISHERIES AND AQUATIC RESOURCES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 443, 454, 463 AND 482 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Rationale: The fisheries sector is now faced with the problem of over-exploitati on of fisheries resources. Large-scale commercial fishing and the use of prohibited means of fishing have resulted in the depletion of fisheries resources, extinction of fish specieis and the destruction of coral reefs. > One major factor which contributed to this problem is the lack of effective government officials at the local level who will help in the formualtion and implementation of policies and programs relating to fisheries and aquatic resources. > Provides, therefore, for the position of FISHERIES OFFICER who will formulate and develop measures, plans, strategies relating to fisheries and aquatic resources.

Official representatives of the country in other international athletic competitions who won gold, silver or bronze medals shall receive a monthly pension for a period not exceeding five (5) years. rows.abstract: Rationale : Many military retirees, who are also considered veterans coming from the different branches of the Armed Forces of the Philippines enjoying benefits provided in R.A. 7696 although they may also be reciving other benefits from the repestice military branch of office.  This Bill aims to correct a situation where, a veteran or a direct descendant may be enjoying both benefits granted by PVAO and the Armed Forces of the Philippines. It is noticeably clear that a substantial amount is saved and preserved if this measure will be implement thereby, the government can utilize the saved portion for some other benefits that may be granted to deserving veterans whose pension allocations are depleted.

rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR THEFT OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS IN THEIR ORIGINAL STATE
rows.abstract: States that --- "SECTION 1. Any person shall commit theft of agricultural products and livestock in its original state including the theft of coconuts from a plantation, and the theft of fish and aquatic resources from fishponds, shall be punished with imprisonment of not less than twelve years but not mroe than twenty years in accordance with the following schedule: (1) Eighteen years to twenty years, if the amount of the crops involved exceeds P2,000.000.00.; (2) Fifteen to seventeen years, if the amount of crops involved exceeds P5,000,000.00 but does not exceed P2,000,000.00.; and (3) Twelve to fourteen years, if the amount of the crops involved does not exceed P5,000,000.00.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 1996-08-07

rows.abstract: Prescribes the COMMUNITY-BASED FOREST ACTION PLAN for this purpose.  A community-based forest management approach recognizes that only with the mobilization and empowerment of the people who have a direct stake in the sustained life of a forest canthe same be protected, rehabilitated and effectively managed.
